stories.headline: Flournoy Wins It Late for THE MACHINES
stories.dek: THE MACHINES 97.82, Killer Klowns 92.14. 10 lead changes, and the last one was the only one that kept.
paragraphs: Now this one I enjoyed, and I enjoy almost nothing. THE MACHINES and Killer Klowns swapped the lead 10 times before one of them finally kept it, and THE MACHINES were the ones holding it when the weekend ran out: 97.82–92.14.

The play that settled it came in the fourth quarter, Monday night: Ryan Flournoy with a 35-yard catch. That put THE MACHINES in front at 94.32–92.14, and for all the traffic that had come before it, nobody took it back. There were 8 touchdowns in this game and the one that mattered went THE MACHINES’s way last.
THE MACHINES moved to 7-0, first in Spartan. Killer Klowns fell to 3-4, fourth in Spartan. THE MACHINES sit first in the league on the full table, 800 points scored.

Trey McBride led the winners with 17.1, and Jared Goff and Amon-Ra St. Brown kept him company. Bo Nix actually outscored every man on the field with 23.7 and still lost, which tells you plenty about the other nine spots.

Killer Klowns will want to look away from this next bit. Caleb Douglas sat on their bench and scored 19.0 while Wan'Dale Robinson held the same slot and returned 0.7 — 18.3 points in a chair, in a game they lost by 5.7. That is not a defeat, that is a self-inflicted wound with a witness.
Somebody put that one on the tape and keep it somewhere safe.

stories.headline: Lil’ Chops Make It Hurt
stories.dek: Lil’ Chops 102.98, Master-Jeti 57.9. It was over long before it was finished.
paragraphs: Some games are contests. Lil’ Chops beat Master-Jeti 102.98 to 57.9, and the 45.1 points between them at the end flatter nobody — Master-Jeti did not lead at any stage of this football game.
There is no sequence to describe, because there was no sequence. Lil’ Chops scored first, kept scoring, and the remainder was arithmetic performed in public.
Lil’ Chops moved to 4-3, second in Spartan. Master-Jeti fell to 3-4 and third straight defeat, third in Spartan.

Dak Prescott led the winners with 25.0, backed by Bucky Irving and Quinshon Judkins, who were not merely present. Braelon Allen finished with 13.4. It will look good in a season summary and it did nothing today.
Master-Jeti started Cade Klubnik and were rewarded with 0.0 points. He was out there. I can confirm he was out there.
A beating, administered and received. Nothing more to add.

stories.headline: BIG BLUE Make It Hurt
stories.dek: BIG BLUE 135.6, Wookie Leaks 85.44. It was over long before it was finished.
paragraphs: This was not a football game, it was a receipt. BIG BLUE beat Wookie Leaks 135.6 to 85.44, and the 50.2 points between them at the end flatter nobody — Wookie Leaks led early, lost it, and never argued again.

They took it in the first quarter — Chase Brown with a 5-yard run, 26.22–26.0 — and then simply never gave it back. 18 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put Wookie Leaks in front again.
BIG BLUE moved to 3-4, third in Black and Blue. Wookie Leaks fell to 2-5, fourth in Black and Blue. Wookie Leaks are fourteenth of 16, and the 668 points conceded is most of the reason.

Joe Burrow led the winners with 31.0, with useful afternoons from Malik Willis and Tee Higgins as well. Tony Pollard actually outscored every man on the field with 33.5 and still lost, which tells you plenty about the other nine spots.
BIG BLUE left Cam Skattebo and his 18.1 on the bench and played Chase Brown in the spot instead, for 5.8. It cost them nothing in the end, which is the best that can be said for it.
File it, forget it, and let us never speak of it again.

stories.headline: Pork Chop Express Win the Last Exchange
stories.dek: Pork Chop Express 120.24, Beaver Eaters 99.88. 7 lead changes, and the last one was the only one that kept.
paragraphs: They could not stop trading punches and I could not stop watching. Pork Chop Express and Beaver Eaters swapped the lead 7 times before one of them finally kept it, and Pork Chop Express were the ones holding it when the weekend ran out: 120.24–99.88.

They took it in the second quarter — Minnesota Vikings with a sack, 46.34–45.06 — and then simply never gave it back. 12 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put Beaver Eaters in front again.

Pork Chop Express moved to 6-1 and fifth in a row, second in Black and Blue. Beaver Eaters fell to 6-1, first in Black and Blue. Pork Chop Express sit third in the league on the full table, 854 points scored.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba did the heaviest lifting — a 28-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, Sunday night, worth 8.8 on its own. Michael Penix Jr. and D'Andre Swift did the rest of the damage. Drake Maye actually outscored every man on the field with 25.0 and still lost, which tells you plenty about the other nine spots.
Both of them earned the night off. One of them gets to enjoy it.

stories.headline: Gumbas Survive the Back-and-Forth
stories.dek: Gumbas 73.16, n.W.o 60.8. 8 lead changes, and the last one was the only one that kept.
paragraphs: If you like your football unresolved, this was yours. Gumbas and n.W.o swapped the lead 8 times before one of them finally kept it, and Gumbas were the ones holding it when the weekend ran out: 73.16–60.8.

The play that settled it came in the third quarter, the Sunday late games: Matthew Stafford with a 3-yard touchdown pass. That put Gumbas in front at 59.22–53.7, and for all the traffic that had come before it, nobody took it back. There were 8 touchdowns in this game and the one that mattered went Gumbas’s way last.
Gumbas moved to 3-4, second in The Four Horsemen. n.W.o fell to 2-5 and third straight defeat, third in The Four Horsemen.
Caleb Williams led the winners with 20.0, with Matthew Stafford and Nick Folk chipping in enough to keep it honest. KC Concepcion Jr. answered with 15.2 and it finished 12.4 short.

n.W.o will want to look away from this next bit. Makai Lemon sat on their bench and scored 12.7 while Christian Kirk held the same slot and returned 0.0 — 12.7 points in a chair, in a game they lost by 12.4. That is not a defeat, that is a self-inflicted wound with a witness.
That is the game selling itself, and it does not need my help.

stories.headline: Horsecollars Leave No Doubt
stories.dek: Horsecollars 123.2, Phins Phag 54.82. It was over long before it was finished.
paragraphs: The scoreboard operator went home early and nobody blamed him. Horsecollars beat Phins Phag 123.2 to 54.82, and the 68.4 points between them at the end flatter nobody — Phins Phag led early, lost it, and never argued again.

They took it in the first quarter — Tyler Shough with a 1-yard touchdown pass, 9.14–7.1 — and then simply never gave it back. 8 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put Phins Phag in front again.
Horsecollars moved to 5-2, first in The Four Horsemen. Phins Phag fell to 1-6, fourth in The Four Horsemen. Phins Phag are sixteenth of 16, and the 721 points conceded is most of the reason.

Zay Flowers did the heaviest lifting — a 48-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 10.8 on its own, though it was Geno Smith who finished with the biggest number at 23.7. Zay Flowers and Jonathan Taylor did the rest of the damage. 17.5 from Omar Cooper Jr., and a long quiet afternoon from the rest of Phins Phag.
The good news is that it is over, and that is the whole of the good news.

stories.headline: Guido Haters Edge Smoke Dragons
stories.dek: Guido Haters 87.56, Smoke Dragons 79.2. 8.4 points in it.
paragraphs: The margin here would fit in a hat. Guido Haters 87.56, Smoke Dragons 79.2, an 8.4-point margin that never seriously came under review.

The play that settled it came in the fourth quarter, Sunday night: Emanuel Wilson with a 21-yard touchdown run. That put Guido Haters in front at 85.36–79.2, and for all the traffic that had come before it, nobody took it back. There were 8 touchdowns in this game and the one that mattered went Guido Haters’s way last.

Guido Haters moved to 2-5, third in Spectre Syndicate. Smoke Dragons fell to 2-5 and fourth straight defeat, fourth in Spectre Syndicate. Smoke Dragons are fifteenth of 16, and the 751 points conceded is most of the reason.

Josh Jacobs did the heaviest lifting — a 25-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, the Sunday late games, worth 8.5 on its own, though it was Kirk Cousins who finished with the biggest number at 18.5. Emanuel Wilson and Josh Jacobs did the rest of the damage. Colston Loveland answered with 12.9 and it finished 8.4 short.
A win is a win. It does not always feel like one.

stories.headline: StillTheCream Make It Hurt
stories.dek: StillTheCream 122.04, The Powers of Pain 80.72. 6 lead changes, and the last one was the only one that kept.
paragraphs: There is a version of this where it stays interesting. This was not it. StillTheCream beat The Powers of Pain 122.04 to 80.72, and the 41.3 points between them at the end flatter nobody — The Powers of Pain led early, lost it, and never argued again.

The play that settled it came in the third quarter, the Sunday late games: Jordan Love with a 14-yard touchdown pass. That put StillTheCream in front at 71.6–65.72, and for all the traffic that had come before it, nobody took it back. There were 14 touchdowns in this game and the one that mattered went StillTheCream’s way last.
StillTheCream moved to 4-3 and fourth in a row, first in Spectre Syndicate. The Powers of Pain fell to 3-4, second in Spectre Syndicate.

Rhamondre Stevenson did the heaviest lifting — a 48-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter, Thursday night, worth 10.8 on its own, though it was Luther Burden III who finished with the biggest number at 19.7. Rhamondre Stevenson and Tre Tucker did the rest of the damage. C.J. Stroud managed 17.5 for The Powers of Pain, which on an afternoon like this one is a lovely painting in a burning house.
The Powers of Pain started Nico Collins and were rewarded with 0.6 points. He was out there. I can confirm he was out there.
Burn the tape. I will bring the matches.
